claims.text: On September 8th UT San Antonio said its researchers developed a self-sustaining, artificial intelligence-powered flood warning system meant to spot dangerous water accumulation at street level.
claims.quote: Researchers at The University of Texas at San Antonio have developed a self-sustaining, artificial intelligence-powered flood warning system designed to spot dangerous water accumulation at the street level.
claims.scope_note: The university's own story, dated September 8, 2026. It names no installation site.

claims.text: The prototype has temperature, humidity, light and precipitation sensing and four optical water-level sensors mounted at varying heights.
claims.quote: The resulting prototype combines temperature, humidity, light and precipitation sensing, as well as four optical water-level sensors mounted at varying heights.
claims.scope_note: Describes the prototype's design, not a measured deployment.

claims.text: The node runs its machine learning on a small chip and judges local flood risk without relying on a central server.
claims.quote: This on-device AI evaluates current and recent sensor data to predict localized, imminent flood risk without relying on a central server.
claims.scope_note: The model is a compressed TinyML model on the node.

claims.text: The university reports 98.82 percent validation accuracy from initial assessments after training.
claims.quote: So far, the AI has performed well, achieving 98.82% validation accuracy in initial assessments post-training.
claims.scope_note: A validation figure from initial assessments after training. The article reports no street or field result.

claims.text: The node charges its own battery from ambient light and runs on a fraction of the energy of a smartphone.
claims.quote: An onboard power chip collects ambient light to charge a built-in battery and backup energy storage units, allowing the device to run indefinitely on a fraction of the energy used by a smartphone.
claims.scope_note: The university's description of the design.

claims.text: When it detects rising water risks it sends radio signals that can travel more than a half-mile through city streets and up to five miles in open areas to a local central hub where emergency teams can monitor conditions.
claims.quote: These low-power signals can travel more than a half-mile through city streets and up to five miles in open areas without needing cell towers or power lines. The data arrives instantly at a local central hub, where emergency teams can monitor conditions from miles away.
claims.scope_note: The ranges are the university's description of the radio technology.

claims.text: At the hub, server software gathers data from many nodes and a second, larger AI model produces a web dashboard with predictive maps for emergency responders.
claims.quote: A second, larger AI model analyzes spatial and temporal patterns across the network to generate an interactive web dashboard with predictive maps.
claims.scope_note: Describes the intended system. The article names no town or agency that runs one.

claims.text: The parts for one prototype sensing station cost roughly $150 to $220.
claims.quote: The total cost of parts for one prototype sensing station ranges from roughly $150 to $220.
claims.scope_note: Parts for one prototype station only. Not an installed or finished-product price.

claims.text: Pan is pursuing patent protection and the team aims to refine the design into a weatherized commercial product for small coastal municipalities, homeowners' associations, agricultural operations and industrial sites.
claims.quote: The team aims to refine the design into a sleeker, weatherized commercial product suitable for deployment by small coastal municipalities, homeowners’ associations, agricultural operations and industrial sites.
claims.scope_note: A stated aim. No dates and no named buyer.

claims.text: Chen Pan said the goal is to get the technology deployed where it is needed most.
claims.quote: “Our ultimate goal is to get this technology deployed where it’s needed most,”
claims.scope_note: A stated goal, which the article does not say has been met anywhere.

claims.text: The project was funded in part by a Texas Coastal Management Program grant awarded by the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration.
claims.quote: This project was funded in part by a Texas Coastal Management Program grant awarded by the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA).
claims.scope_note: Funding statement from the university's story.

claims.text: The university says some people could have ankle-deep water in their yard by the time a flash flood warning sounds on their phone.
claims.quote: That means some people could have ankle-deep water in their yard by the time a flash flood warning notification sounds on their phone.
claims.scope_note: The university's framing of the problem, not a measured case.

claims.text: The university says existing commercial flood-monitoring stations come with drawbacks, from prohibitively high costs to reliance on grid power or frequent battery replacements.
claims.quote: Existing commercial flood-monitoring stations also come with drawbacks, from prohibitively high costs to reliance on grid power or frequent battery replacements, which leaves them vulnerable during multi-day storms or power outages.
claims.scope_note: The university's characterization of existing stations.

claims.text: Chen Pan said the system is an off-grid solution that generates its own power and evaluates flood risk locally on the device.
claims.quote: Our system is an off-grid solution. It generates its own power, evaluates flood risk locally right on the device and sends timely warnings without needing external electricity or expensive network lines.
claims.scope_note: A researcher's statement about the design.

claims.text: The university story is dated September 8th, 2026.
claims.quote: September 8, 2026
claims.scope_note: Dateline on the university story, above the byline Audrey Gray.

claims.text: The university says custom server software at the central monitoring site gathers data from many nodes across a town or watershed.
claims.quote: At the central monitoring site, custom server software aggregates data from multiple deployed nodes across a town or watershed.
claims.scope_note: Describes the intended system. The article names no town that runs one.

claims.text: The university says the flood-path view helps emergency responders decide on dispatching crews, closing dangerous roads or issuing targeted neighborhood warnings.
claims.quote: This flood-path visualization supports emergency responders as they make crucial decisions, such as dispatching crews, closing dangerous roads or issuing targeted neighborhood warnings long before floodwaters peak.
claims.scope_note: Describes intended use. No responder agency is named.

claims.text: The university says the node uses TinyML, which compresses machine learning so it can run on small, low-power microcontrollers.
claims.quote: Pan’s system sidesteps this roadblock by using TinyML — a branch of computer science that compresses machine learning algorithms so they can run directly on small, low-power microcontrollers.
claims.scope_note: The university's definition of the method.

claims.text: The university says Pan is currently pursuing patent protection for the hardware architecture.
claims.quote: Pan is currently pursuing patent protection for the hardware architecture.
claims.scope_note: A stated pursuit of protection. No grant is claimed.

claims.text: Pan said the dashboard assesses risk levels and shows how flooding could spread across monitored locations, highlighting higher-risk zones so local officials can act quickly.
claims.quote: The dashboard assesses risk levels and shows how flooding could spread across monitored locations, highlighting higher-risk zones so local officials can act quickly.
claims.scope_note: A researcher's description of the intended dashboard. The article names no town or agency that runs one.
